item.title: Fashion Briefing: Meta is auto-generating AI ads for its advertisers, causing headaches for image-conscious fashion brands
item.description: Despite opting out of every possible AI feature Meta offers, one fashion brand found that Meta had started to use AI to alter 5% of the ads that a given advertiser puts out on the platform.

item.title: Luxury Briefing: Joseph returns to the London Fashion Week runway amid a different fashion economy
item.description: For this week’s Luxury Briefing, I spoke with Joseph CEO Barbara Campos about the brand's reentry into London Fashion Week, following years of financial repair and product discipline. The brand arrives at a moment when the middle of the luxury market is redefining its place, as customers shop for quality.

item.title: A buyer’s take on London Fashion Week, with Mytheresa’s Tiffany Hsu
item.description: On this week’s London Fashion Week episode, senior fashion reporter Zofia Zwieglinska is joined by Tiffany Hsu, chief buying director at Mytheresa, for a buyer’s perspective on Fall 2026.

item.title: Glossy Pop Newsletter: Why a beauty brand is giving Gen Alpha equity
item.description: Evereden is not the first brand to give equity to creator partners — Glossy Pop reported on Nudestix's "CSOP" (celebrity stock option plans) in 2022. But the three creators that are a part of its new Generation E, equity-based program are ages 14, 15 and 17 — so they may be among the youngest to receive equity in an established beauty brand.

item.title: Nuuly is leading the fashion rental resurgence, with 70% of its subscribers being new to the market
item.description: Key to Nuuly's success hasn't been taking existing market share away from other rental platforms. Instead, nearly 70% of all Nuuly subscribers have never rented from any platform before, according to Nuuly's customer research. That means Nuuly has succeeded in expanding the addressable market and creating a new cohort of renters.

item.title: Creator marketing is becoming a loyalty play
item.description: As influencer fees compress and algorithms shift, brands like American Eagle and Gap are building always-on advocacy platforms that merge loyalty mechanics with performance-driven creator marketing.

item.title: ‘The perfume houses of tomorrow are scaling up today’: Matiere Premiere’s CEO on priming the brand for global expansion
item.description: When Caius von Knorring, Aurélien Guichard and Cédric Meiffret launched Matiere Premiere in 2017, $25 million in sales was about the ceiling for a successful niche perfume brand. Now, with niche fragrance a billion-dollar business and global expansion on the horizon, Matiere Premiere has its eye on becoming one of the perfume giants of tomorrow.

item.title: How Schwarzkopf is winning pop culture, from Sarah Pidgeon’s CBK transformation to Alysa Liu’s halo hair
item.description: Showing up in the right pop culture moments is paramount for heritage hair brand Schwarzkopf Professional. Most recently, this includes Sarah Pidgeon’s Carolyn Bessette Kennedy transformation for FX’s “Love Story,” earned through a partnership with celebrity hair colorist Kari Hill, and Alysa Liu’s halo hair refresh ahead of her Olympics win. Glossy sat down with Schwarzkopf GM Michelle Chandler to learn more.

item.title: Beauty Briefing: Why everyone wants a piece of Carolyn Bessette Kennedy
item.description: This week, I checked in on the beauty brands and consumers tapping into CBK’s ‘90s style — and the brewing pushback. Additionally, Charlotte Tilbury shakes up its C-suite, and Summer Fridays expands to fragrance.

item.title: On takes aim at Lululemon with proof-first leggings strategy
item.description: As Lululemon worked to contain fallout from its second, January 2026 see-through leggings controversy, On moved into the category with a $120 pair of SenseTec tights. The product boasted the brand's biggest material innovation for 2026.
